name: Hedgehog
group: Animals > Mammals > Wild animals on land > Eats mostly insects

features.claim: A hedgehog is covered with spines on its back.
features.quote: Hedgehogs are easily recognized by their spines, which are hollow hairs made stiff with keratin.

features.claim: A hedgehog has between 5000 and 7000 spines on its back.
features.quote: It has between 5000 and 7000 spines on its back.

features.claim: A hedgehog's spines are usually brown with pale tips.
features.quote: Hedgehogs are usually brown, with pale tips to the spines, though leucistic 'blonde' hedgehogs are found on the Channel Island of Alderney.

features.claim: A hedgehog has a snout like a pig's.
A hedgehog has a furry face, feet and belly.
features.quote: Hedgehogs roll into a tight spiny ball when threatened, tucking in the furry face, feet, and belly.

features.claim: A newborn hedgehog is blind and its quills are covered by a protective membrane.
features.quote: Newborn hoglets are blind, with their quills covered by a protective membrane which dries and shrinks over several hours, and falls off after cleaning, allowing the quills to emerge.

not_this.claim: A hedgehog's spines are not barbed like a porcupine's quills.
not_this.quote: Their spines are not poisonous or barbed and, unlike the quills of a porcupine, do not easily detach from their bodies.
